title: Epic Sepsis Model external validation at Michigan Medicine
system_purpose: Proprietary sepsis early-warning score embedded in the Epic EHR that alerts clinicians when a hospitalized patient may be developing sepsis
decision_impact: Alert is meant to trigger clinician review and consideration of sepsis workup/treatment; a missed alert delays recognition, a false alert consumes clinician attention
affected_groups: hospitalized patients;treating clinicians;hospital sepsis response teams
verified_facts: Peer-reviewed external validation at Michigan Medicine (27,697 patients; 38,455 hospitalizations; Dec 2018-Oct 2019) found the Epic Sepsis Model had AUC 0.63 at the hospitalization level and only 33% sensitivity at the clinically used alert threshold, missing 67% of confirmed sepsis hospitalizations while alerting on 18% of all hospitalizations.
reported_harm: Confirmed technical performance finding from a peer-reviewed study, not an allegation: the high false-negative rate is a foreseeable hazard of delayed sepsis recognition/treatment, and the high alert burden is a foreseeable hazard of alert fatigue degrading clinician response to future real alerts.
quantitative_evidence: AUC 0.63 (95% CI 0.62-0.64); 33% sensitivity at the deployed threshold; alerted on 18% (6,971/38,455) of hospitalizations; missed 67% (1,709/2,552) of confirmed sepsis hospitalizations; about 8 patients evaluated per true sepsis case.
limitations: Single-site retrospective validation at one academic health system; does not itself document a specific patient death or injury, only that the alerting logic under-detects sepsis and over-alerts relative to the developer's reported performance; may not generalize to other hospitals, EHR configurations or later model versions.

title: IBM Watson for Oncology unsafe/incorrect treatment recommendations
system_purpose: AI-based clinical decision support tool intended to recommend cancer treatment options to oncologists
decision_impact: Recommendations are intended to inform an oncologist's treatment-selection decision for a cancer patient
affected_groups: cancer patients;oncologists;hospitals that licensed the tool
verified_facts: STAT News reported that internal IBM Watson Health slide presentations from 2017 documented 'multiple examples of unsafe and incorrect' cancer treatment recommendations, and that the system was trained on synthetic/hypothetical cases curated by a small number of Memorial Sloan Kettering specialists rather than on real patient outcomes or broad clinical guidelines.
reported_harm: Reported by internal company sources and customer feedback cited in leaked documents, not a regulator finding or court judgment: a foreseeable hazard of oncologists receiving unsafe treatment suggestions, not a documented case of a specific patient injury.
quantitative_evidence: Source does not publish a denominator or population size for 'multiple examples'; no public count of affected patients or hospitals is available in this reporting.
limitations: Based on leaked internal slide decks and journalist sourcing, not a peer-reviewed study or regulatory audit; cannot confirm how many real patients received unsafe recommendations in production, nor document a specific patient outcome.

title: Babylon Health symptom-checker chatbot triage accuracy dispute
system_purpose: AI symptom-checker chatbot used to triage patient-reported symptoms and suggest possible conditions/next steps within the GP at Hand telehealth service
decision_impact: Chatbot's suggested triage/possible-condition output can influence whether a patient seeks urgent care versus routine follow-up
affected_groups: patients (gender-bias allegation specifically affecting women);GP at Hand telehealth users;treating clinicians
verified_facts: TechCrunch reported that oncologist Dr. David Watkins, testing the chatbot over three years, documented cases where it failed to flag potential heart attack symptoms in female patients while suggesting panic attack or depression, and that Babylon Health's own rebuttal analysis counted 20 cases as 'genuine errors' among a disputed number of test triages.
reported_harm: Allegation from one clinician's independent testing, publicly disputed by the vendor, not a regulator finding or confirmed patient injury: a foreseeable hazard of gender-based under-triage of cardiac symptoms delaying urgent care for female patients.
quantitative_evidence: Disputed count: Babylon states about 20 genuine errors out of about 2,400 self-reported tests (about 0.8% error rate by Babylon's framing); Watkins disputes the test count as closer to 800-900 complete triages, which would imply a meaningfully higher error rate; no independent, regulator-audited error rate is public.
limitations: Relies on one clinician's self-directed, non-randomized testing plus a company-authored rebuttal; the denominator and resulting error rate are actively disputed by both parties; not a controlled clinical trial or independent regulator audit.
